1.plain: Two sides sit past the 80° valve and two sit under it. Iran 79° (6.9 — unchanged: the rial firmed 100 to 230,800 at the Monday open, a hair off the score; the 'struck in 7 days' component stays 6 with nothing hit since Qeshm on Sep 16; the talks component stays 'signals only' — Naqvi is due in Tehran today with, Baghaei says, no US message, Araghchi is in Doha on his way to New York, and Ghalibaf's 'no return to the previous negotiation framework until the Americans fulfil their commitments' is a statement; the IRGC's claim of 'another' MQ-1 destroyed over the strait is a single-region claim and enters no component; regime 6.0, no Gulf act against Iran) — the 07:00 crossing below the valve is still Sam's call. US 82° (7.3 — unchanged: the door component edged up as Brent bounced from a $101.71 low to $102.2; Reuters/Ipsos 35% is the approval input, 'fired' 7 on the Sep 14–15 MQ-1s until Sep 22, the election component 6.33 at 44 days — still above the valve, no crossing; Waltz's 'maximum pressure' is the only US-government word overnight). Saudi–UAE 84° (7.6: 'struck' already 10 on the Taif death; the Italian-jet hit cannot raise it; revenue unresolved). Small Gulf 75° (6.6), below the valve for a ninth day — the crossing is still held. If the rial firms, Iran's next mechanical step down is 6.8 at ~228,000; one confirmed US strike on an Iranian asset puts it back to 7.3; Brent back above ~$104 lifts the US pot to 7.4, and a fall to ~$92 would take it to the valve.
1.trade: Brent touched $101.71 at 02:13 GMT (lowest since Sep 10) and was back at $102.2 by 06:06 UTC — the diplomacy discount is being tested against a new IRGC drone claim; the 10-yr reprices at the US open; Polymarket 'Iran–Oman agreement by Sep 30' at 30% is the line to watch through Naqvi's Tehran visit and Trump's Tuesday speech.

2.plain: The door is quiet and three sources now say so: Sep 20 closed at 6 in / 14 out with 53 hulls in the strait — the tenth day in a row under ten inbound; UKMTO's weekly assessment says its independent tracking shows 'single-digit numbers transiting in both directions' against the US NCAGS figure of more than 30 a day; and Reuters, citing Kpler, counts 12 commodity vessels through the strait on Saturday and Sunday against 35 the weekend before (five out on Saturday with agricultural cargo, LPG and fertiliser, one empty gas carrier in; four out on Sunday, two small oil tankers in), with the caveat that Gulf producers 'continue to export oil on tankers travelling with their transponders off'. CENTCOM's Cooper said on Saturday that oil, cargo and LNG volume these past two weeks is 'higher than at any point in the past six months' and the primary lanes are 'clear of mines'; Shekarchi calls the billion-barrel figure 'false and ridiculous'. Nothing new was struck at sea (UKMTO's list still ends at #139, held; CENTCOM's press index still ends Sep 15); the IRGC's claim of 'another' MQ-1 destroyed over the strait on Monday morning is a single-region claim with no US word. The AIS poller counts 14 crossings in the 24 h to 06:00 UTC Sep 21 (4 in, 10 out — two oil/chemical tankers of 84,715 dwt, two bulk carriers, a container ship and the small LPG/chemical tanker out; a 46,187-dwt chemical tanker, a general cargo, a cargo vessel and a tug in) with 589,913 bbl of petrochemical exports and no crude, 1,285 ships in the two gulfs; Sep 21 has 25 hulls inside after six hours. PortWatch still ends Sep 13 at a 7-day average of 5.3 commercial transits — seven days behind at the Monday open. The live layer at 06:01 UTC: 167 aircraft, 1,314 ships, all tiles OK; no military flag in either bucket; one unnamed US-military MLAT hex over the eastern UAE, none over Iran.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Thirty-seven items wait for Sam's tick — NOTHING new at Sep 20 23:00. The Monday-morning candidate is the IRGC's claim that its air defences destroyed 'another' US MQ-1 over the strait (Press TV 05:19 UK; Al Jazeera carries the claim): it is single-region — no CENTCOM word, no US official to a Western outlet, nothing on UKMTO — so it sits in the weak table and in the 72-hour list as a claim, exactly as the army's 'Orbiter' did on Sunday; the Sep 14–15 MQ-1s only became a rung-8 proposal (18 03:00-3) when CBS's US officials confirmed them, and this one would follow the same path on a Western or CENTCOM confirmation, as a separate event. Otherwise restatements: Waltz's 'maximum pressure … door open in good faith' and Haji Deligani's 'remaining in the NPT brings us nothing but losses' are statements; Baghaei says Naqvi brings no US message; Araghchi is in Doha. The talks thread (11:00-1 and the three earlier items) waits on Naqvi's arrival and any US official on the record; the tanker rungs and the MQ-1 rung 8 hold at ~81 hours of CENTCOM silence; the Riyadh rung (19 11:00-1/-2) still leans to rejection; the Italian-jet rung (20 07:00-1/-2) has no Rome or Riyadh update; the Iran valve crossing (20 07:00-3) is unchanged at 6.9 on a rial of 230,800.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days: Iran seizes or fires on a tanker; a Gulf energy strike is the second card; the Oman MOU track is the third — and two held signals (the UAE crown prince's meeting, Bahrain's refusal) would move the deal card up and the widen-the-war card up respectively if ticked.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill: gas, yields, rial.
7.trade: DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: whether CENTCOM or a US official confirms the IRGC's 'another MQ-1' (the Sep 14–15 drones took two days to reach CBS) — and whether Iran shows imagery of either drone; whether Naqvi arrives in Tehran today with a US message (Rezaei: mediated talks 'under way') or only 'bilateral relations' (Baghaei, twice); what Araghchi hears in Doha before New York, and whether any US official confirms Qatar's 'assurances' on the record; whether Waltz's 'good faith' door and Trump's 'probably' survive to a Pezeshkian slot, and whether Tuesday's speech (Iran's bomb) or the six Gulf-leader meetings come first; whether Ghalibaf lets the NPT-withdrawal bill out of the Presiding Board before or after New York; whether the deputy speaker's 'energy blockade' becomes policy; whether the Armed Forces HQ's 'backing of some regional countries' is ever matched by a Western report of a coalition; whether PortWatch's Monday publication of Sep 14–20 settles the count now that UKMTO, Reuters/Kpler and the board's AIS agree against NCAGS/Cooper; whether the Tehran Times' 'unprecedented visa bans' on the UNGA delegation are confirmed by State; whether the Houthis' 'blockade for blockade' spares US and third-flag hulls in practice; whether Riyadh ever attributes the airport fuel-depot fire; whether Brent's bounce from $101.71 holds through the US open; what USNI's Monday tracker says about which US hulls are still inside the Gulf.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

tiles.trade: Brent: pressure ≥7 on all three pots has coincided with +8–12% moves inside 2 weeks (Mar, Jul); if any pot drops below its line, expect Brent −5%

tiles.counter: definitions: Stuck = no signed deal, no regime change, door under 30 ships/day, fighting continues; Signed deal = a signed US–Iran agreement (not an MOU, not a pause); Regime change = any leadership change in Tehran, including an IRGC takeover or Khamenei succession; Bigger war = US or Israeli strikes on Iranian territory sustained over a week, or a Gulf-wide exchange, or US ground forces engaged; Strait regime = passage resumes ≥30 ships/day under Iran–Oman rules or fees, no war, no signed deal; Other = anything else (Houthi Red Sea closure, US unilateral pause, etc.)

tiles.counter: Covers official accounts only (central banks, sovereign funds), not hedge funds or UK banks, and only what is custodied at the New York Fed — a central bank moving paper to Euroclear shows as a sale here without selling. It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.
tiles.moves: Every Thursday evening: append the new Wednesday level (the 19:00 run); a weekly drop above $30B is the alert line; cross-check with Japan MoF weekly securities flows (Thursday) when available
tiles.trade: Custody −$134B since end-April with the 30-yr at a 20-year high = official selling into a bear-steepener; a week of +$30B or more after an intervention has marked the local top in yields twice (Jul 29, Aug 26)

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Bush CSGs and the Boxer ARG in the Arabian Sea, Lincoln departed for Thailand Sep 2 · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
